    Rajya Sabha returns SC Judges' Bill to Lok Sabha after consideration

    Rajya Sabha returns The Supreme Court (Number Of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026 to Lok Sabha after consideration.

  • rajya sabha
    August 05, 2026 16:30
    Consultation process on over SC Benches in south India: Law Minister

    Tracing the process over negotiations to constitute regional Supreme Court Benches, Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal referenced Article 130 of the Constitution of India which allows the Supreme Court to sit in Delhi or other places chosen by the Chief Justice of India with the approval of the President.

    He also mentioned writ petitions that have been considered over the last few years and said that the government believes in the independence of judiciary. “The consultation process is on,” he added.

  • rajya sabha
    August 05, 2026 16:21
    Soon we will see a woman Judge as CJI: Law Minister

    Hitting out at MPs “who overlook the positive aspects”, Law Minister Arjun Meghwal said India will soon see a woman Judge as the Chief Justice of India. 

    The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill replaces an ordinance promulgated earlier this year to raise the sanctioned strength of the apex court from 34 to 38 judges, including the Chief Justice of India. After the ordinance, one more woman SC judge was added, Mr. Meghwal stated.

    Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the government is particular about Nari Shakti Abhiyan, the Minister added.

  • rajya sabha
    August 05, 2026 16:10
    Law Minister Arjun Meghwal replies to discussion on SC Judges' Bill

    Union Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal highlighted the need for structural shift the higher judiciary, i.e. the Supreme Court. He even took the example of the Sabarimala case which is being heard by a nine-Judge Bench, leaving lesser judges available for other cases.

    The government says the increase will enable the Supreme Court to hear more cases simultaneously, thereby improving the disposal rate. 

    One of the arguments in favour of additional judges is that it will make it easier for the Chief Justice of India to constitute Constitution Benches on a regular basis. The Constitution Benches, comprising at least five judges, hear cases involving substantial questions relating to the interpretation of the Constitution. Because of the heavy daily roster, constituting such Benches has often proved difficult.

    Several Rajya Sabha members calls for increase of judges' strength in HCs and trial courts

    Speaking during the discussion on the SC Judges’ Bill in the Rajya Sabha, several MPs from across party lines spoke in favour of the Bill and also stressed that the strength of the Judges’ needs to be increased even in high courts and trial courts.

    Further, several MPs raised the issue of case pendency, calling for reforms that ensure speedy justice for all citizens across the country.

    Lok Sabha passes Bill on banker's books without debate

    Amid relentless Opposition protests, a Bill to include digital and virtual records as admissible evidence in the courts was passed in the Lok Sabha on Wednesday (August 5, 2026) before the proceedings were adjourned for the day.

    Lok Sabha passes Bill on banker's books without debate

    Congress MP Rajeev Shukla alleged that the Rajya Sabha Chair has started “dictating” what a member can say or not.

    “Everyone was speaking on the Bill (Supreme Court Amendment Bill, 2026) today. Now, a situation has arisen where the Chair has started dictating what you can and cannot say. Never before in the history of Parliament has it happened that you are told during a speech, ‘No, you must say only what we want; you cannot speak about anything else.’ The Opposition has been left with no voice at all... this is the height of dictatorship,” he said.

Today, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju met us to discuss delimitation and to know the stand of the Opposition. Our stand on delimitation is very clear.     Will increasing number of judges guarantee justice: JMM MP asks

    Jharkhand Mukti Morcha MP Mahua Majhi, speaking during the SC Judges’ Bill discussion, asked whether increasing the number of Judges will guarantee justice. She said that India’s justice system needs a complete overhaul and also depends on the kind of people running the system.

    She also highlighted the plight of thousands still waiting for justice due to various factors including pendency of cases and the lack of accessibility to even district courts, let alone the Supreme Court.

    BRS MP Ravichandra Vaddiraju pitches for a 'South India Bench' of SC in Hyderabad

    Rajya Sabha MP from BRS party Ravichandra Vaddiraju, speaking in favour of the SC Judges’ Bill, urged the government to consider a SC Bench “for South India” to enhance accessibility to justice and the judges.

    He further said Hyderabad is the best suited location for such a bench that will help citizens avoid extra hassle and costs in coming to New Delhi for all SC cases.

    Rajya Sabha continues discussion on SC Judges' Bill; AAP's Sanjay Singh supports

    The Rajya Sabha continues discussion on the SC Judges’ Bill even as several Opposition MPs stages a walkout.

    AAP MP Sanjay Singh, who spoke in favour of the Bill, was appreciated by Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju in a lighthearted moment. Further, Mr. Rijiju clarified a point raised Mr. Singh on inclusion of people from SC/ST communities in the Supreme Court. The Union Minister said that the government has no role to play in the collegium system used to appoint SC judges.

    Lok Sabha adjourned for the day amid Oppn. protest

    Shortly after passing the The Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill, 2026, the Lok Sabha was adjourned for the day. The House will next meet at 11 a.m. on Thursday (August 6, 2026).

    The Bill, passed through a voice vote without discussion, seeks to provide a law relating to evidence with respect to bankers’ books and align it with contemporary digital banking practices, along with matters connected or incidental thereto.

He claimed the Congress, CPI and the Samajwadi Party have always opposed Lord Ram, and that their “chanda chori” skit in the Parliament premises has hurt sentiments.

    “They should apologise to the country,” he said.

    Further, Mr. Rijiju also accused the Opposition of not wanting the House to function. “K.C. Venugopal is a good man, but he is unable to make his party members understand maintain decorum,” Mr. Rijiju told the House, adding that the government is up for a discussion. “I urge the members to not impose matters.”

    Referring to the ongoing student protests in Jharkhand, he took a few Opposition MPs’ names and asked them to go to Ranchi and speak up on matters related to exam “irregularities”.

    Rajya Sabha takes up SC Judges' Bill discussion amid Oppn. protests

    Amid repeated requests to maintian decorum of the House, the Rajya Sabha took up the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026, for consideration and passing.

    It was passed by a voice vote in the Lok Sabha on August 3.

    The Bill amends the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956 to increase the number of puisne (ordinary) judges from 33 to 37. With the CJI included, the court’s sanctioned strength rises from 34 to 38.

    Independent MP Pappu Yadav on Wednesday (August 5, 2026) launched an attack on BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj, claiming that her primary objective in public life appears to be initiating legal actions against Congress leader Rahul Gandhi.

    Speaking to reporters Mr. Yadav said, “As for Sushma Swaraj’s daughter (Bansuri Swaraj), it appears that she was born only to file cases against Rahul Gandhi. She goes to the police station whenever she wishes. She has no understanding of the law.”

    Congress MP K.C. Venugopal said Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju met the Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, “with the government’s agenda, with the Prime Minister’s agenda”. 

    “Parliament exists for debate and discussion. They do not want any debate or discussion. They want to bulldoze everything. They want to pass separate legislation, which we cannot agree with at all. That is what happened today...” he added.

    “Solution has to be given by the government. We are raising the issue. Students were brutally assaulted by the Delhi police. AK-47 was being used in Bihar. There should be an answer from the Home Minister of India. Why is he running away? Like ‘chanda chori’, Ram Mandir. There is no answer. We are asking only for a discussion. What happened in Ram Mandir donation? These people who are so-called ‘bhaktas’, now completely are stealing the money of Lord Rama. There is no accountability, there is no investigation, proper investigation,” Mr. Venugopal said.

    PM Modi interacts with 37 BJP MPs over breakfast meeting

    Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday (August 5, 2026) hosted a breakfast meeting with 37 BJP MPs at his residence as part of his ongoing interactions with parliamentarians during the Monsoon session of Parliament.

    During the meeting, the Prime Minister is said to have shared personal experiences and held informal discussions with the MPs. Those who attended the meeting included newly elected party leaders Tarun Chugh and Vinod Tawde and former AAP leaders Swati Maliwal, Raghav Chadha, Ashok Mittal, Sandeep Pathak and Vikramjit Singh Sahney.

    The breakfast meeting during Parliament sessions has been part of the prime minister’s practice for several years, providing the MPs an opportunity to directly interact with him.

    The breakfast meeting was part of the Prime Minister’s practice of meeting different groups of BJP MPs during Parliament sessions to interact and exchange views.

    The ruling party also accused the Congress leader of making “baseless” remarks against the BJP and the RSS.

    The remarks came after Mr. Gandhi on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) said the students of the country are in “severe pain” and they do not need Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s forgiveness but his apology for his government’s action against them.

    If you want good services, you need to pay for it: Nitin Gadkari

    On a question on charges at toll plazas by DMK’s P. Wilson, Mr. Gadkari elaborated on the FASTag or Unified Payments Interface (UPI) process by the government. He said the government is looking to change the whole system by eliminating toll nakas and enuring a smooth process.

    “If you want good services, you need to pay. Everything cannot be provided for free,” he said, in his answer.

    Under the National Highways Fee Rules, vehicles entering a toll plaza without a valid and functional FASTag are charged twice the applicable user fee if they pay in cash. However, highway users who choose to pay via UPI are charged 1.25 times the user fee for their respective vehicle category.

    Later, Chairperson Radhakrishnan makes a request to the Union Minister, urging him to make provisions of a pass to former MPs to travel without toll on the highways, similar to the one provided by the Railways.

    AAP's Sanjay Singh moves Rule 267 notice in Rajya Sabha against mandatory E20 fuel

    Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) MP Sanjay Singh on Wednesday (August 5, 2026) submitted a notice under Rule 267 in the Rajya Sabha, seeking a discussion on the public outrage and consumer rights issues arising from the mandatory implementation of E20 petrol ahead of the Monsoon Session in Parliament.

    “The government has advanced its ethanol-blending target from 2030 to 2025 and has effectively made E20 petrol the default fuel available at a large number of retail outlets (petrol pumps) nationwide. Consequently, millions of citizens are being compelled to use a fuel for which their vehicles were neither designed nor certified, all without any meaningful alternative or informed consent,” he said.

    He noted that the Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari admitted in Parliament that E20 petrol results in a 2-6% reduction in fuel efficiency (mileage), depending on the vehicle type and age.

    “This admission is significant as it establishes that consumers are forced to purchase more fuel to cover the same distance. Lakhs of vehicle owners across the country have reported a noticeable drop in mileage, a decline in engine performance, increased maintenance costs, and concerns regarding long-term engine durability. These apprehensions are no longer merely hypothetical,” he said.

    ANI

    Parliament clears Bill for stronger birth, death registration rules

    The Rajya Sabha on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) passed The Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill, 2026 amid protests by Opposition members demanding an apology from Union Home Minister Amit Shah for the police action against student protesters. The Lok Sabha too had cleared the Bill on Friday (July 31, 2026) without any major debate. The Bill proposes to amend sub-section (3) of Section 13 of the present Act to make provisions of delayed registration more stringent.

    Parliament clears Bill for stronger birth, death registration rules

    Rajya Sabha passes Registration of Births and Deaths Bill amid Opposition protests.

    Manickam Tagore seeks debate on Jantar Mantar police action

    Congress MP Manickam Tagore B also submitted an adjournment motion notice in the Lok Sabha, seeking a discussion on the police action during a student protest held at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on July 20 and demanding a statement from Union Home Minister Amit Shah on the incident.

    In his notice, Mr Tagore said that reports and allegations arising from the incident had raised serious concerns about the nature and proportionality of the force used to disperse the protesters.

    “Reports and allegations arising from the incident have raised serious concerns regarding the nature and proportionality of force used to disperse the protesters. It has been alleged that lathi charges, pellet guns, tear gas, and water cannons were used against students, including women participants, resulting in injuries and widespread public concern. These allegations require a full, fair and transparent examination,” the notice reads.

    -ANI

    Manish Tewari seeks Lok Sabha debate on Anti-Defection law

    Congress MP Manish Tewari submitted an adjournment motion notice in the Lok Sabha, seeking suspension of the day’s listed business to discuss the need for a new anti-defection law to curb mass political defections.

    In his notice, Mr. Tewari sought leave to move a motion for the adjournment of the House to discuss what he described as a matter of “definite urgent public importance.”

title: Zuckerberg apologises for child sexual abuse material, deepfake content, say sources
author: Aroon Deep,Nistula Hebbar
content_html:
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg conveyed his “apologies” for child sex abuse material (CSAM) content, “deepfake content and errors in operating the platform,” government sources said after Joel Kaplan, the tech giant’s global head of public policy, met with officials from the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology on Wednesday (August 5, 2026).

Mr. Kaplan said in a statement that he apologised to the government on Meta’s behalf. “Meta will be called again,” the sources said, indicating that further meetings are on the slate. The delegation led by Mr. Kaplan also met IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw.

Mr. Kaplan had been summoned, among other things, to explain why Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s first video message to the youth posted on July 23 was temporarily removed from Facebook. The company has since said that this was done in error. The government had insisted on a full accounting of the error and a personal apology from Mr. Zuckerberg. The sources’ readout of the meeting did not include a specific reference to that post’s takedown.

The meetings follow heightened concerns around Instagram’s role in amplifying the protests at Jantar Mantar last month, which include Mr. Modi’s brief post removal on Facebook. Government officials asserted that Meta is “not covered under the Intermediary definition,” a significant statement, since this would make the company liable in court for every single post by users. The government also dressed down the company on a BBC report on ads appearing on Instagram promoting CSAM.

The official sources added, “They select who receives the content. Safe harbour under IT Act not applicable. They admitted that a lot of money was paid for boosting certain type of content. They apologized and regretted the mistake … Meta accepted the mistake that a lot of illegal content was promoted. Paid promotion carried out for specific audience.”

Meta did not comment on the meetings.

Standing committee

Earlier in the day, according to a letter from the Lok Sabha Secretariat, Parliament’s Standing Committee on Communications and Information Technology, headed by the Bharatiya Janata Party’s Nishikant Dubey, demanded that Google India’s safe harbour be lifted, thereby leaving the firm liable for individual users’ posts as a publisher. The letter, seen by The Hindu, cited cybercrime complaints in Hyderabad where complainants lost over ₹48 lakh due to cyber frauds from apps downloaded from Google Play, where Google’s India country manager was named as a co-accused.

This follows a similar demand for Meta, where the committee sought the withdrawal of Instagram’s safe harbour following the brief takedown of Mr. Modi’s video. The committee also cited the reporting on child sex abuse material (CSAM) advertisements on Instagram.

The letter was addressed to IT Secretary S. Krishnan and copied to Home Secretary Govind Mohan. The IT Ministry and Meta did not have an immediate response to a query on the letter when contacted by The Hindu. Google declined to comment.

“During the deliberations, the Committee demanded an apology from Mr. Mark Zuckerberg, Meta Chief, on this issue,” the Committee wrote in the letter. “If he fails to tender an unqualified apology within 3 days of receipt of this letter, the protection/immunity given under Section 79(3) of IT Act may be withdrawn and action taken against him as a Publisher.”

Section 79 of the IT Act, 2000 says that “an intermediary shall not be liable for any third party information, data, or communication link made available or hosted by” them, subject to certain conditions. The IT Rules, 2021 are the main way those conditions have been expanded by the government, including requirements of taking down content upon notice by law enforcement agencies or designated government officers.

It is unclear if safe harbour can be revoked by the government. “There is no express legal provision under the present legal framework through which the Government can directly remove or revoke the safe harbour protection provided to intermediaries under Section 79 of the IT Act,” law firm Scriboard’s founder Ravi Goyal told The Hindu.

“Moreover, the safe harbour protection provided under Section 79 is not a blanket or platform-wide immunity and instead applies in relation to specific content or instances. Therefore, even if an intermediary is found not to be entitled to such protection in respect of a particular piece of content or instance, it could still continue to avail the protection under Section 79 for its services, subject to compliance with law. Thus, such actions are determined on a case-to-case basis by a court of law.”

At a hearing where Meta, Google and X (formerly Twitter) representatives were speaking in front of the committee on Monday (August 3, 2026), MPs from the Opposition pushed back against the ruling party’s line of questioning, saying content moderation on social media platforms should not be subject to political influence.

title: Is abusive language a criminal offence in India? | Explained
author: Rizmi Lia M.
content_html:
The story so far: Following protests by the Cockroach Janta Party at Jantar Mantar, multiple FIRs were registered against demonstrators over the use of allegedly “abusive and objectionable language”.

Among them was a Zero FIR, which allows a complaint to be registered at any police station regardless of where the alleged offence occurred. It was lodged at the Expressway Police Station in Uttar Pradesh on the complaint of a Ghaziabad resident. The FIR invokes Sections 352 (intentional insult to provoke breach of peace), 353(1) (statements conducive to public mischief), and 356(1) (defamation) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), alleging that the remarks were intended to “spread hatred and disrupt public peace”.

The case once again raises a recurring legal question: Is using abusive language, by itself, a criminal offence in India?

What provisions of the BNS deal with abusive speech?

The BNS does not criminalise abusive language as a standalone offence. Whether abusive speech amounts to a crime depends on its nature, context and consequences.

Section 352 of the BNS, which corresponds to Section 504 of the erstwhile Indian Penal Code (IPC), deals with intentional insult with intent to provoke a breach of peace. It penalises intentional insults only when they are made with the intention, or knowledge, that they are likely to provoke the person insulted into breaking the public peace or committing another offence. Mere abusive language, without these ingredients, does not automatically attract the provision. The offence is punishable with imprisonment of up to two years, or with fine, or both.

Where abusive language is accompanied by threats to a person’s life, reputation or property, Section 351, dealing with criminal intimidation, may apply.

Section 353, corresponding to Section 505 of the IPC, criminalises statements, rumours or false information made with the intent, or likelihood, of causing public mischief. This includes statements intended to incite offences against the State, disturb public tranquillity, or provoke one community against another.

Section 356(1), corresponding to Section 499 of the IPC, deals with criminal defamation. It applies where a person makes or publishes an imputation concerning another with the intention, knowledge or reason to believe that it will harm that person’s reputation.

The BNS also recognises several exceptions to criminal defamation. These include imputations that are true and made for the public good; fair criticism of the public conduct of public servants or any person involved in a public question; publication of substantially true reports of court proceedings; fair criticism of public performances; censure passed by a person having lawful authority; accusations made in good faith before a competent authority; imputations made in good faith to protect one’s own or another’s interests; and cautions issued in good faith for the benefit of the recipient or the public.

Additionally, where abusive words, gestures, sounds or acts are directed at a woman with the intention of insulting her modesty, Section 79 of the BNS, corresponding to the erstwhile Section 509 of the IPC, may be attracted.

What have the courts said?

In State of Telangana v. Nalla Balu @ Durgam Shashidhar Goud (2026), the Supreme Court upheld operational guidelines framed by the Telangana High Court for police authorities and Judicial Magistrates dealing with criminal proceedings arising from social media posts and public speeches.

The Court held that the police cannot mechanically register FIRs merely because someone finds a social media post or public speech offensive or insulting. This applies even where allegations relate to promotion of enmity, intentional insult, public mischief or threats to public order. An FIR should be registered only where there is prima facie material indicating that the speech amounts to incitement to violence, hatred or public disorder.

The Court further observed that police should not routinely invoke criminal law against harsh, offensive or critical political speech. Only where the speech amounts to incitement to violence or poses an imminent threat to public order can criminal prosecution be justified. Constitutional protection of political speech under Article 19(1)(a) must be scrupulously enforced.

The Supreme Court had earlier, in Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015), held that mere annoyance or offence caused to others is not a constitutionally permissible ground to restrict free speech. Only speech amounting to incitement to imminent violence or public disorder may attract criminal sanction. Read in this constitutional framework, Section 352 must be interpreted narrowly and applied with restraint.

Courts have also drawn a distinction between obscenity and language that is merely abusive or vulgar.

In Mani @ Subramaniyam v. State, represented by the Deputy Superintendent of Police (2026), the Supreme Court held that obscenity is not synonymous with vulgarity, abuse or profanity.

“Legally, obscenity is not synonymous with vulgarity, abuse or profanity. Mere swear words, profanities and vulgar expletives, however distasteful or uncivil, cannot be equated with obscenity,” the Court observed.

The Court held that the test of obscenity is whether the words are lascivious, appeal to prurient interests, or tend to deprave and corrupt impressionable minds. It must also be shown that their use caused annoyance to others. Unless these essential ingredients are established, the offence of obscenity under Section 296 of the BNS, dealing with obscene acts and songs in public places, is not made out.

The Bench further observed that words may be insulting, offensive or unpleasant without necessarily being obscene in law. While vulgar or abusive language may evoke disgust, shock or revulsion, that alone does not make it criminally obscene.

The distinction was also emphasised by the Supreme Court in Mohammad Wajid & Anr. v. State of Uttar Pradesh & Ors. (2023). The Court said that mere abuse, discourtesy, rudeness or insolence may not amount to an intentional insult within the meaning of the law.

Each case involving abusive language, the Court said, must be decided on its own facts and circumstances, and there can be no general proposition that merely using abusive language against a complainant would never amount to an offence under Section 504 of the IPC.

Abusive language, by itself, is not a standalone criminal offence under the BNS. Depending on the context, however, it may attract provisions relating to intentional insult, criminal intimidation, public mischief, defamation or offences against women. Courts have consistently held that criminal liability depends not on the mere use of offensive or vulgar language, but on whether the statutory ingredients of the offence are satisfied in the facts of each case.

title: States cannot cite financial burden to oppose raising retirement age of judicial officers: Supreme Court
author: PTI
content_html:
Observing that States cannot cite financial burden to oppose raising the retirement age of judicial officers, the Supreme Court on Wednesday (August 5, 2026) asked State governments to revisit the issue of enhancing the age of superannuation of judges and decide within two weeks.

A Bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said concerns of financial burden are "misconceived".

"We impress upon all the state governments to revisit the issue of enhancement of the age of retirement of judicial officers, irrespective of the age of superannuation prescribed for other government employees," the Bench said.

The Supreme Court said retaining experienced judicial officers may impose a lesser financial liability than retiring them and filling the resulting vacancies.

"We have no reason to doubt that the continuation of experienced and seasoned judicial officers would entail a lesser financial liability than what the State would incur upon their retirement.

"The reasons assigned by the State governments for declining to enhance the age of retirement are, therefore, untenable. However, we are of the considered opinion that the larger issue should be resolved through consensual measures," the Bench said.

Also read: SC issues notice to Madhya Pradesh, HC registry on plea for enhancing retirement age of judges

In its order, the Supreme Court said the issue shall be revisited on an urgent basis and an independent and pragmatic decision shall be taken within two weeks.

"In the event a State government decides to enhance the age of retirement, the benefit of such decision shall also be extended to judicial officers who retire during the intervening period," the Bench said.

The Supreme Court had earlier asked the States and Union Territories to consider raising the age of superannuation of judicial officers from 60 to 61 years.

Uniform enhancement of retirement age

The Bench was hearing a petition seeking uniform enhancement of the retirement age of district judiciary judges from 60 to 62 years across the country.

"All State governments and Union Territories (UTs) are directed to take a decision, in consultation with their respective jurisdictional high courts, on this issue. In case they agree, judicial officers in such states shall be permitted to continue in service up to the age of 61 years. Such continuation shall remain subject to the final outcome of these proceedings," the bench ordered.

While the retirement age of Supreme Court judges is 65, the high court judges superannuate at the age of 62 years.

The issue arises against the backdrop of the Supreme Court's 2002 judgment declining to accept the recommendation of the Justice K. Jagannatha Shetty Commission, which had proposed raising the retirement age of district judges to 62 years.

Since then, some States, including Telangana and Madhya Pradesh, have moved towards increasing the retirement age.

On November 20, 2025, a Bench headed by the then CJI B.R. Gavai, since retired, had raised the retirement age of judicial officers of Madhya Pradesh from 60 to 61 years.

The Bench, in its interim order, had referred to a similar decision taken by the Telangana High Court.

It asked why judicial officers should be denied the relief when the State government was willing to do so.

title: Kozhikode youth alleges abduction, blackmail by six-member gang
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
The Chevayur police have registered a case based on a complaint by a 21-year-old who alleged that he was abducted, confined, and blackmailed by a six-member gang during a visit to Bengaluru. The complainant alleged that the group recorded private videos of him and demanded ₹8 lakh, threatening to circulate the footage if he failed to pay.

The police have launched an investigation with the assistance of the cyber cell and are examining digital evidence, including mobile phone records, to identify the accused.

According to the complaint, the youth, a resident of Kozhikode, travelled to Bengaluru on July 24 to meet a friend and stayed at the latter's flat. He alleged that a group took him outside on the pretext of introducing him to another acquaintance.

The complainant said he was later taken to an isolated location and held there for a week. He alleged that the group recorded videos of him without his consent and sent the footage to his family members.

According to the complaint, the gang later demanded ₹8 lakh and threatened to release more videos if the money was not paid. The complainant said he managed to escape and return to Kerala, following which he approached the Chevayur police.

Police sources said the accused included a woman and five others. Preliminary inquiries indicated that all the suspects were from Kozhikode district and that the motive behind the alleged abduction could be established soon.

title: Inscriptions key to tracing Karnataka’s cultural links with neighbouring states: Kannada varsity VC
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
A two-day State-level workshop on “Kannada inscriptions in Karnataka and beyond,” organised by the Centre of Excellence for Studies in Classical Kannada (CESCK) under the Department of Higher Education at the Central Institute of Indian Languages (CIIL), Mysuru was inaugurated on Wednesday.

Inaugurating the programme, Prof. D.V. Paramashivamurthy, Vice-Chancellor, Kannada University said, “This workshop will facilitate a comparative study of the cultural and historical ties between Karnataka and regions outside the State. Inscriptions found in Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, and Kerala are crucial for understanding ancient Karnataka’s cultural linkages, art, architecture, and administration with neighbouring States.”

“Most inscriptions discovered in Karnataka are Dana Shasanas. These records provide evidence that grants were given not merely for ritualistic adherence, but to uplift the underprivileged. Detailed studies are needed to ascertain if similar grant inscriptions exist in neighbouring States,” the Vice-Chancellor suggested.

He stressed the need for examining whether the acts of sacrifice, heroism, hunting traditions, political affairs, and religious developments expressed in Kannada inscriptions are reflected in other regions.

“Inscription texts help us understand the prevalent religions and sectarian conflicts of the era and carry out comparative analysis. Through this workshop, the Centre of Excellence for Studies in Classical Kannada has set the stage for re-evaluating these records by bringing together prominent epigraphists from across South India,” he added.

Srinivas Padigar, a retired professor from Dharwad, who was the chief guest and gave a presentation featuring inscriptions from various historical sites, including the ‘Sri Utpatti Pidugu’ inscriptions at the Kudaveli Sangameshwara Temple in Alampur (Andhra Pradesh), the Jalasangi Kallesheshwara Temple in Bidar, the Kedareshwara Temple in Dharmapuri, and the Kailasanathar Temple in Kanchipuram. While these inscriptions have been published by the Kannada University, Hampi in the volumes of ‘Kannada Inscriptions of Andhra Pradesh’, certain errors remain in those publications that require editorial correction, he advised.

CIIL Director Basavaraja Kodagunti, highlighted the need for analysing inscriptions systematically.

Highlighting the vital role of inscriptions in reconstructing the long history, culture, and literature of Kannada, L.R. Prem Kumar, Coordinator, Classical Languages, said, “From Halmidi inscription of 450 CE to the inscriptions at Talagunda, Badami, Atakur, and Dekabbe, we can trace the evolution of the Kannada script, language, and poetic structure.”

“As described in Kavirajamarga—from the Kaveri to the Godavari— the influence of Kannada extended well beyond the modern borders of Karnataka. Owing to the cultural impact of the Chalukya, Rashtrakuta, Hoysala, and Vijayanagara dynasties, Kannada inscriptions are found in Kurkyala (Telangana), Thanjavur (Tamil Nadu), Maharashtra, Goa, Madhya Pradesh, and as far as Nepal.”

The organisers said the workshop serves as a key step toward reassembling these historical links and rediscovering the language’s historical expanse.

N.M. Talawar, Project Director of the Centre of Excellence for Studies in Classical Kannada, along with staff members of the Classical Kannada Institute, epigraphy enthusiasts, and scholars were present.

title: Bihar woman alleges panchayat blamed her for rape, public humiliation
author: Amit Bhelari
content_html:
A 30-year-old woman in Begusarai district has alleged that after being raped by her neighbour, she was subjected to public humiliation instead of receiving justice.

According to her complaint, villagers caught the accused while he was allegedly trying to flee by breaking a window. They then convened a village panchayat and allegedly humiliated her in front of those present. A purported video showing the woman doing so went viral on social media.

As per the FIR, lodged on Saturday (August 1, 2026), the mother of two children was allegedly raped twice on June 2 and 4, 2026, when her husband, who works as a labourer in another State, was away from the village. The woman lodged the complaint after her husband returned to the village on June 25.

According to the complaint, the FIR was filed after the purported video of the incident went viral on social media, triggering widespread outrage. The complaint states that during the panchayat on July 5, 2026, she was asked to hold her ears and kneel, and was allegedly forced to lick her own spit after the village panchayat declared that it was all her fault.

Speaking to The Hindu, Deputy Superintendent of Police (Headquarters), Begusarai, Nikhil Kumar, said, “Police have lodged the FIR based on the complaint of the woman. The incident took place two months back, in which she has alleged that she was threatened by the accused and raped. When the accused was trying to flee the house by breaking the window, the villagers caught him.”

He further said, “Both the accused and the woman were subjected to humiliation. However, in the complaint, she has not mentioned the name of any individual. One video is getting viral on social media; police are trying to verify the authenticity of that video and investigation is underway.”

The incident took place under the jurisdiction of the Ballia police station. When contacted, Sub-Divisional Police Officer (SDPO), Ballia, Subodh Kumar, said one person, who is the son of a ward councillor, had been arrested in the case.

According to police sources, the accused is known to the woman and is also a distant relative.

title: Kalaburagi: District Science Centre to observe Hiroshima Day with educational programmes
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
The District Science Centre, Kalaburagi, will observe Hiroshima and Nagasaki Day on August 6 and 7 by organising a series of educational programmes for school and college students to create awareness about the devastating human and environmental consequences of the atomic bombings.

According to a press release issued by the District Science Officer, a documentary screening on the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki and an exhibition of a nuclear reactor model will be held at 11 a.m. on August 6.

On August 7, an interactive science awareness lecture will be delivered by Mr. Balaji Biradar, assistant professor, Department of Physics, S.B. Science College, Kalaburagi, at 11 a.m. An open-house science quiz on the theme ‘Energy’ will also be organised.

For further details, interested persons may contact the District Science Centre, Kalaburagi, on 08472-270608 or 9788078048, the release said.
